task: Teach the existing release-risk subsystem classifier that canonical src/lib/instances/** tenancy authority is a high-risk auth/access surface, so tenancy changes are not unresolved by Plan Before Code.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This changes the existing release-risk classification policy, not product behavior. It must classify canonical tenancy code without broadening unrelated paths or weakening risk limits.

acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/instances/** is classified by the existing release-risk policy as auth-access-authority.
The mapping does not alter risk scores, limits, or any other subsystem definition.
The canonical DOMAIN-TENANCY ownership remains unchanged; the release policy only classifies verification risk.
A deterministic test proves the mapping exists and remains isolated.
invariants: No new quality system or subsystem is introduced.
The existing auth-access-authority high-risk classification is reused.
Domain truth ownership and release-risk classification remain separate concerns.
No product/runtime file changes in this prerequisite.

failureModes: The classifier leaves canonical tenancy files unresolved and blocks legitimate tenancy development.
An overly broad pattern accidentally classifies unrelated src/lib code as high-risk auth/access.
edgeCases: Nested tenancy files under src/lib/instances subdirectories are included.
No other subsystem receives a new pattern.

alternatives.summary: Introduce a new release-risk tenancy subsystem.
alternatives.reason: That would create a new parallel quality classification and require unnecessary policy/dependency expansion.

alternatives.summary: Add src/lib/instances/** to the existing high-risk auth-access-authority subsystem.
alternatives.reason: Tenant selection is security-sensitive access context and this resolves the missing classification using the existing risk model.

specialistReviews.finding: Release-risk classification must not redefine domain truth ownership.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep DOMAIN-TENANCY unchanged and only map src/lib/instances/** into existing auth-access risk classification.

specialistReviews.finding: Changing release policy inside the same high-risk tenancy feature violates isolation and inflates the release-risk budget.
specialistReviews.resolution: Ship this policy mapping as an isolated prerequisite release unit before reconciling the tenancy feature.

challenge.scenario: A future tenancy file is added under src/lib/instances/subdir/file.ts.
challenge.finding: The classifier must recognize nested canonical tenancy paths.
challenge.resolution: Use the existing glob form src/lib/instances/** rather than one-file entries.

challenge.scenario: The policy edit accidentally changes score thresholds or another subsystem.
challenge.finding: That would be a broader release-governance change than required.
challenge.resolution: Test exact presence of the one pattern and assert policy limits/subsystem names remain unchanged.

challenge.scenario: The mapping is interpreted as moving tenant truth into DOMAIN-IDENTITY.
challenge.finding: Risk classification and architecture authority serve different concerns.
challenge.resolution: Do not edit domain-foundations; preserve tenant-context-authority as canonical owner.

proofPlan: Add a deterministic regression test for the exact src/lib/instances/** mapping and unchanged DOMAIN-TENANCY ownership.
Run full Quality Tests, TypeScript and Production Build.
Require exact-head Completion Truth and lifecycle closure before merging the prerequisite.

requirements.requirement: The existing release-risk classifier recognizes canonical src/lib/instances/** tenancy authority through the existing high-risk auth-access subsystem without changing domain ownership or risk limits.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Release-risk score or subsystem limits are not weakened.

notes: Isolated prerequisite extracted from Stage 1 platform tenant-context work after Release Risk Budget correctly rejected combining release-policy classification with the high-risk product change.
